featured_reviews.review_text:
Long Post Alert!

Women's Hospital "Room Harmony" has been etched in my memory as it  was my home for two and a half months.
I had a complicated pregnancy and was advised completed bed rest and was admitted under Dr. Gayatri Rao's guidance who turned my hope into reality. She is the sweetest soul who would brighten my dark days with her encouraging words and smile.
On April 2nd, I delivered a premature baby boy after the long tiring journey.
I would also like to thank the nurses who had made my stay homely with utmost care and positivity. They were nice to me and somehow became my friends by the time I was leaving.
A big shoutout to sisters - Vidya, Hema, Trishala, Smita, Mayuri, Namrata, Alpa, Yashika, Sunita and I might have missed few other names but I am equally grateful to each.

Not only the nurses even the maushis were accomodating everytime I had to use the loo as I was on complete bed rest.

Last but not the least, I would also love to mention few other doctors who helped me with the littlest difficulty, doubt, concern even during the middle of the night namely Dr. Dipali, Dr. Vijaya, Dr. Shalini, Dr. Surti and Dr. Dolly.

Dr. Dipali was very empathetic soul who would keep visiting my room and appreciating and encouraging me to overcome each day in the hospital. Dr. Vijaya would flawlessly put the IV drip's on me with most care and concern avoiding any chances of hurting me. Also, Dr. Manju sinha would keep visiting and advising me to read books for a positivity.

Another appreciation I would want to give the phlebotomist who would come for my blood tests and would tell me lovingly that I would be a good mom. I forgot her name but I hope you guys will find out who she is.

It was a tumultuous journey for both me and my husband, but the way Dr. Gayatri Rao made my pregnancy possible with her positive smile and golden words is beyond everything.

It was a long stay but it became bearable with each and every person mentioned above. Thank you guys, for helping me out during the most fragile yet memorable time of my life. I will always be indebted to this hospital.

The only drawback if I may mention are the charges of the hospital as it is located at the posh side of bandra khar. But, for middle class people like us the charges were indeed challenging.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience.

My experience at Ramakrishna Mission Hospital was deeply unsatisfactory and alarming. For an institution associated with such a respected name, the overall standards of care, hygiene, and management are far below acceptable levels.

The trainee doctors displayed an arrogant, careless, and dismissive attitude, lacking basic empathy and professionalism. Patient concerns were often brushed aside, creating unnecessary stress and frustration.

Cleanliness is a major issue throughout the hospital. Washrooms and patient areas were unhygienic, poorly maintained, and visibly dirty, raising serious concerns about infection control and patient safety.

Despite booking and paying for a “First Class” room, the condition was horrible and unacceptable—dirty floors, stained and broken tiles, poorly maintained toilets, foul smell, and an overall neglected environment. This was misleading and completely unworthy of a first-class facility.

Time management is extremely poor. Long waiting hours, lack of communication, and no respect for patients’ time indicate weak administration and poor coordination.

The only positive aspect of this hospital experience was the professionalism and dedication of Dr. Ulhas Nadkarni and Dr. Amarish Warty. Both doctors were knowledgeable, patient, and compassionate, and they treated us with respect and genuine care. Their conduct reflects what medical professionalism should look like.

Unfortunately, apart from these two doctors, the hospital suffers from poor hygiene, unprofessional trainee behavior, misleading facilities, and inefficient management. Immediate corrective action is required.

I would not recommend this hospital unless serious improvements are made.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m writing this review with a broken heart. My mother-in-law is no longer with us, and I believe DR. SALMAN ALI SAYED (Nephrologist) at this hospital is responsible.
He misdiagnosed her condition - or failed to diagnose it properly at all. Her health deteriorated rapidly under his care. What could have been treated became fatal because of medical negligence.
We trusted this doctor with someone we loved. We believed he would help her. Instead, we lost her.
The rushed appointments, the failure to listen to our concerns, the lack of proper and unnecessary testing - it all added up to a tragedy that didn’t have to happen. This hospital treated her like a SOURCE of REVENUE, not a HUMAN BEING fighting for her life.
She’s gone now. Our family is shattered. And I have to live every day knowing that better care could have saved her.

To anyone reading this:

PLEASE get a second opinion. Ask questions. Demand answers. Don’t trust blindly like we did.

If this review saves even one person from what we went through, then maybe her death won’t be completely meaningless.

We will never get her back. Don’t let this happen to your family.

After collecting the case paper, we went to the ward for the check-up. The nurse asked us to fill out a form, but her behavior was extremely rude. It is not possible to explain everything properly to the patient alone.

When my wife showed her the reports, the doctor said, “These are old reports, bring new ones.” My wife politely asked the doctor to please check the date, as they were the latest reports. After checking, the doctor had no answer and went silent.
Is this really the level of professionalism expected from doctors at such a reputed hospital?
This entire experience was extremely disappointing. A hospital of this level should focus on basic respect, patient dignity, and proper communication. The staff and doctors seriously need training in behavior and patient handling.

I came to this clinic with a swollen foot and another health concern, expecting at least a basic examination. No proper inspection, no questions, nothing.

Later it turned out that the foot was actually fractured, which makes that quick visual diagnosis even more impressive.

I also brought the bottle of a prescription medication I’ve been taking for years, clearly labeled with my name, simply asking for a refill while traveling. Despite knowing me for less than five minutes, the doctor confidently informed me that I “shouldn’t take it” and refused to prescribe it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
had a very disturbing experience at Beams Hospital during tests for my infant. As a parent, you trust a hospital with the most important thing in your life—your child’s health. Unfortunately, our experience left us extremely concerned about the accuracy and reliability of the testing process.

Some of the test results we received appeared inconsistent and raised serious doubts about whether the samples were handled and processed correctly. When dealing with infants, precision and care in diagnostics are absolutely critical. Any inaccuracies can lead to unnecessary stress for parents and potentially incorrect medical decisions.

I strongly urge the hospital administration to review their laboratory procedures, quality checks, and communication with parents. Families rely on hospitals to provide accurate and trustworthy medical care, especially for newborns and babies.

I hope improvements are made so that other parents do not have to go through the same anxiety and uncertainty we experienced.

Saifee Hospital is a Dawoodi Bohra founded multi-speciality hospital at Charni Road, Mumbai, India, overlooking the Arabian Sea. Saifee Hospital is founded by the head of the Dawoodi Bohra faith, Syedna Mohammad Burhanuddin, dedicated the hospital to the memory of his revered father, Syedna Taher Saifuddin.
History:-
Saifee Hospital was established by the Dawoodi Bohras in 1948 with the aim of providing safe, ethical and affordable medical assistance to people of all faiths and socio-economic backgrounds. In 2000, the foundation of a new hospital on the existing premises was laid down by Dr Syedna Mohammed Burhanuddin. Construction commenced in 2001 and the new hospital was commissioned on 4 June 2005 in the presence of the Prime minister of India, Dr. Manmohan Singh. The architecture of the hospital features a combination of classical Arabian (with domes and arches) and contemporary (with glass curtain facades) styles.
Services:-
The hospital has approximately 257 beds, as well as 44 ICU beds, and 9 operating theaters, and conducts over 10,000 surgeries a year.
Saifee Hospital specializes in bariatric surgeries, cardiology, critical care medicine, dentistry, dermatology, gynecology, hepatology, oncology, neurology, nephrology, ophthalmology, neonatology, high dose radioactive therapy units, and Pressurized Intra Peritoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy (PIPAC). The hospital features a highly advanced Robotic Surgical System to facilitate the surgeon in performing complex but minimally invasive surgery.
In the aftermath of the 2011 Mumbai bombings, Saifee Hospital provided free treatment to victims and others affected by the bomb blast.
